searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he mission — make search discovery a real public door the awtsmoos reveals no doorway through an imagined url; awtsmoos.com must answer in public truth, with crawlable torah flowing from root to route. user visible mission turn the current local seo work into a real production capability on canonical main: https://awtsmoos.com/sitemap.xml must return real xml, not 404. https://awtsmoos.com/robots.txt must return real crawler guidance. /heichelos/sitemap.xml must be a fast useful seed map, not an expensive recursive computation. heichel and series html must expose ordinary crawlable links. numeric road routes must server render the real torah teaching before javascript. canonical named post urls must remain stable and indexable. nonexistent posts must remain non indexable. broad possibilities considered 1. static root sitemap plus dynamic heichel sitemap. 2. one giant recursive dynamic sitemap. 3. per heichel recursive sitemaps. 4. generated sitemap artifacts during deploy. 5. search index driven sitemap generation. 6. fast seed sitemap plus semantic html graph traversal. 7. root dynamic routing for robots/sitemap. the rejected deep recursion designs already proved capable of 30–120 second timeouts and server monopolization. the strongest practical architecture is a real static root sitemap plus a fast privacy filtered heichel seed sitemap, while server rendered html links reveal deeper series and named posts. release reality the local branch is main. local committed head is ahead of freshly fetched origin/main. seo changes remain modified/untracked in the shared working tree. production currently returns 404 for /sitemap.xml, proving the local work was never activated publicly.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he first critique — what can still go wrong the awtsmoos demands evidence before confidence may rise; awtsmoos.com must not trade one missing door for a fragile surprise. risks shared working tree contains unrelated changes from other agents. origin/main is behind local committed main; a release must preserve the canonical local main lineage without staging unrelated dirty files. root static .txt and .xml mime support must be committed with the feature or production may serve weak content types. sitemap routes must be ordered before generic /:heichel routes. sitemap generation must reuse canonical public/discoverability policy and avoid private/test heichelos. deep synchronous sitemap recursion must remain deleted. numeric road aliases must not appear as sitemap canonical urls. post and heichel templates must consume pre rendered semantic fragments rather than fragile nested template includes. production deployment must activate an exact pushed sha and then be verified from the public origin. verification obligations source readback; isolated clean worktree diff review; js syntax/import checks; xml parse tests; relevant route tests; isolated server raw http acceptance; public production http acceptance; final branch/origin/production sha reconciliation.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he second critique — real door, not decorative xml the awtsmoos opens a door only when a crawler can walk through what it names; awtsmoos.com therefore needs discovery links, canonical documents, and production truth in the same frame. improvement over the earlier sitemap idea the sitemap is not the entire crawl graph. it is the seed. the real crawl architecture is: robots.txt → root sitemap + heichel seed sitemap → public heichel roots → server rendered child series links → server rendered child series / stable named post links → server rendered torah article with canonical metadata this avoids giant recursive sitemap latency while still making the torah graph discoverable through standard links. release architecture because the shared main worktree is dirty, create an isolated worktree from the current local main commit—not from stale origin/main. copy only the reviewed seo files into that release worktree. test there. commit there on a temporary release branch. then fast forward local main to that exact commit only if its original head has not diverged unexpectedly. push main after a fresh fetch/fast forward ancestry check. this preserves every existing committed local main change while excluding unrelated uncommitted work.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he final execution plan the awtsmoos moves from hidden source to tested vessel to public light; awtsmoos.com shall not call the work complete until the canonical domain answers right. 1. inventory exact seo delta against current local main and origin/main. 2. re read every seo source file and the canonical release scripts. 3. determine exact ship set and dependencies; reject planning artifacts from release. 4. create isolated release worktree from current local main head. 5. copy whole seo files into isolated worktree only. 6. verify isolated status lists only approved paths. 7. run syntax, import, xml, targeted tests, and diff checks. 8. run isolated server acceptance covering robots, root sitemap, heichel sitemap, heichel hierarchy, series named post links, road ssr/canonical/noindex behavior. 9. fresh fetch origin/main; prove origin remains an ancestor of release lineage. 10. commit exact release files. 11. fast forward local main to release commit without touching unrelated dirty files. 12. push main to origin. 13. deploy exact pushed sha through the repository's canonical production release path. 14. verify public awtsmoos.com crawler endpoints and target road with direct http and independent web fetch. 15. update remaining work, planned vs actual delta, and final release evidence.
